name: Settings
summary: How to organise a settings surface — group ordering, help-text vs tooltip, sub-settings, plan-gating, and the danger zone — built from existing components.
lead: Settings is the most-repeated surface in the product, so it drifts fastest without shared rules. This pattern ships NO new component: it reuses Checkbox, Button, Icon and the --aha-size* spacing scale, and documents the CONVENTIONS that make every settings panel read as one product. The narrative 'why' lives in the aha-design-settings skill; this artifact carries only what the repo can enforce.

skillRef.note: The skill is the source of truth for rationale, worked BAD/GOOD examples, and the full 52 SETTINGS-xx assertions. This pattern distils the enforceable subset and links each rule back by ref.

surfaceChoice.useFor: per-object settings, immediate effect on canvas
one-time action or short flow, not independently persisted

composedOf.use: grouped options saved together; consent
the danger-zone CTA (danger variant → colorError)
the ? help glyph, drag handle, per-option image, delete — functional icons only
the whole spacing hierarchy (4/8/16/32/48) — separation comes from spacing, never dividers
danger CTA colour — never hardcode a hex
a single setting that takes effect immediately (toggle rows)
duration/unit/mode dropdowns; recommended default pre-selected
text/number fields; NumberWithUnit for a number + unit
the ? help tooltip (HelpTooltip) — shared dark-navy tooltip, arrow anchored to the ? icon
the reusable form of this pattern — SectionHeader (semibold group header) + SettingRow (label left / control right, or stacked) rendered from a schema over DS controls; spacing-only hierarchy
DropdownMenu — themed action menu (aha-dropdown + aha-menu) for image Change/Edit/Delete and Improve-style menus
the aha-menu inside DropdownMenu's action menu — neutral-grey item hover
ModeField — a labelled field whose input swaps with an inline exclusive mode control (outline radio group / segmented); only the active mode's body is live
CountedInput — single-line field with a focus-only char counter (counter is a persistent sibling revealed via :focus-within, never a remount-on-focus)
CountedTextarea — multi-line sibling of CountedInput; grows between minRows/maxRows, same focus-only counter
CardSelect — single-select as an icon+label card grid; the one selection shape Ant has no built-in for
NumberWithUnit — digit input + hover stepper (clamped, maxDigits) + unit-in-full + optional error line, at an 8px corner; for durations/numbers-with-a-unit
OptionRow — repeatable option/answer row: drag handle, optional correct toggle, borderless textarea with hover counter, optional image control, floating delete
NumberedItem — repeatable numbered SECTION wrapper for composite items (chip + '<Label> N' header + hover delete + grey container); body is a slot
QuestionList — editable list of collapsible questions (prompt field + OptionRow choices); composes NumberedItem/OptionRow
ImageDropzone — full-width settings-only image field (dashed card, empty/loading/filled) emitting intents; the host runs the upload modals, never a self-built uploader
ImageActionButton — per-option image control with empty/loading/thumbnail states + Change/Edit/Delete menu; emits intents
InfoBox — settings-only tinted callout (information/success/warning/error), optionally dismissible with persisted state; bespoke, not Ant Alert

componentBacklog: The atomic controls this pattern composes (Switch, Select, Input, Tooltip=HelpTooltip, Dropdown=DropdownMenu) and the DS's own <aha-settings-list> (SectionHeader + SettingRow + SubSettingGroup) ship today. The composed settings-lab controls that the DS does NOT yet ship as first-class artifacts — ModeField, CountedInput, CountedTextarea, CardSelect, NumberWithUnit, OptionRow, NumberedItem, QuestionList, ImageDropzone, ImageActionButton, InfoBox — are tracked here as backlog: each is a full composite (contract + lib + parts + conformance) and should be authored in the DS so a fully-compliant settings surface is buildable by reuse. See the canonical settings-lab → DS mapping in parts/settings.guide.md.

rules.rule: Setting name is a short noun phrase — no leading verb (Enable/Allow/Show/Turn on). The control communicates the action; the label names what is acted on.
Toggle when the change takes effect immediately; checkbox when options are saved together as a group or express consent. Never mix toggles and checkboxes in one group.

Help text only for a must-see consequence that is hard to undo (≤90 chars, states the consequence). Default is ZERO help lines per panel; everything else is a ? tooltip or nothing. Never both channels on one setting.

The help trigger is a question-mark (?) glyph from the shared Icon — never an info circle (ⓘ). Every ? in a panel is the same glyph, size, and tooltip placement; the tooltip is the shared dark-navy tooltip with its arrow anchored to the icon.
Hierarchy and separation come from --aha-size* spacing tokens (4 name→help, 8 sub→parent, 16 sibling, 32 group, 48 danger zone) — never divider lines, never raw px.

Plain settings and groups sit directly on the panel surface, separated by spacing — never wrapped in a card or tinted/bordered container. Card styling is reserved for genuinely selectable items and the repeatable composite-item wrapper.

A group has 2–6 settings. Header is a 1–3 word noun phrase, sentence case, no colon. Only the group header carries weight — semibold (600, the SectionHeader weight); member/single-control labels are regular weight (400).

Build a settings surface by reusing the canonical composed controls — SectionHeader, SettingRow, SubSettingGroup, HelpTooltip, ModeField, CountedInput/CountedTextarea, NumberWithUnit, CardSelect, OptionRow, NumberedItem, QuestionList, ImageDropzone/ImageActionButton, InfoBox, DropdownMenu — mapped to their DS form (parts/settings.guide.md). Never hand-roll a settings control that already exists in the library; a control the DS does not yet ship is a tracked backlog gap (composedOf), not licence to re-implement it privately.

A dependent sub-setting is HIDDEN (not disabled) when its parent is off. When shown it reads as nested — indented and de-emphasised — never as a top-level peer and never bracketed by its own separators.
A plan-gated setting stays visible but locked (crown badge) — never hidden. The badge opens the shared Paywall popover (owned by aha-design-paywall), not a bespoke one.

Dangerous/irreversible settings sit last, set apart by the largest gap (48). The CTA is the danger Button (colorError, no hardcoded hex); red never on the label. Any irreversible action requires a confirmation modal.

A narrow control sits inline with its label (label left / control right); a wide control (textarea, wide select, radio group, image dropzone) drops below it. Never stack a narrow control or cram a wide one inline.
Every object occupies only its real content height. A container that renders nothing visible is removed or collapsed to zero — never left holding space (the #1 source of editor mystery-gaps).

reuseNote: Doc-only pattern — ships no composition wrapper from this repo. The canonical composed settings controls live in slide-type-creator's @/iframe/settings library (ui-standard.json → settingsLibrary is their source of truth); parts/settings.guide.md carries the explicit, one-per-component mapping from each library control to its DS form (a DS contract, a documented convention, or a tracked backlog gap in composedOf). As each backlog control graduates into this DS it gets a contract + reuse block and is gated like a composite; when the DS ships it, flip its composedOf entry from missing→available and move the mapping row to 'mapped'.

selfCheck.label: names are noun phrases, no leading verb
help text near-absent; ? tooltip carries elaboration
separation via spacing tokens, no dividers/containers
